item.title: Polish Access to Island Studies: A Literary Perspective | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Tomasz Mizerkiewicz, Yinhui Mao. Contemporary Polish literature reveals a significant shift in Polish representations of islandic experiences, with imaginative travels to islands gradually being replaced by records of personal encounters.

item.title: Mapping Decolonial Futures: Imagining Islands Beyond the Colonial Gaze | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Cara Flores, Josephine Chambers & 2 more. Through thinking with and learning from island ontologies, we aim to conceptualize and illustrate how mapping islands marks coloniality as well as how we could subvert colonial cartographic traditions.

item.title: Generation of Digital Sense of Place in a Mediatized Society: Reconstruction of Human-Island Relations on Shamian Island, Guangzhou | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Xiaohua Li, Junyi Wang. When interacting with the place, individuals continuously strengthen their own roles and participate in reproducing the local image.

item.title: Measuring Accessibility Within Islands | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Vania Licio, Anna Maria Pinna. Exploring the dynamics of marginality and geographic peripherality at the island level, focusing on accessibility within Italy’s two largest islands, Sicily and Sardinia, and exploring their internal variability.

item.title: Liquid Landscapes: Water Tunnels, Flamingos, and Radar Sounds in Contemporary Photography From Cyprus | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Elena Stylianou. Through a decolonial lens, and using Cyprus as a case study, the paper examines how contemporary photography and artistic practicesare re-making islands by reclaiming alternative local perspectives.

item.title: Exploring Drivers of Traveler Loyalty for Small Island Destinations | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Heesup Han, Pipatpong Fakfare & 4 more. Using cumulative prospect theory, we establish and test research models to examine underlying determinants and risk factors of tourist loyalty such as motivation, the theory of planned behavior, and image.

item.title: The Role of Local Shops in Emergency Logistics and Island Resilience: A Case Study From Zhoushan Archipelago | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Huan Zhang, Lei Shi & 1 more. Local shops, such as convenience stores, are critical for strengthening island distribution networks and supplying necessities, particularly during emergencies.

item.title: Everyday Gendered Spaces of Memory, Community, and Resistance in Sakaemachi Market (Okinawa) | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Ayano Ginoza, Francesc Fusté-Forné. This paper explores the role of local food markets in the planning and development of complex and dynamic everyday gendered spaces that contribute to island resilience and sustainable development.

item.title: "Not Your Climate Refugees": A Maldivian Perspective on Migration and Adaptation | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Robert Stojanov, Ilan Kelman & 1 more. Islanders tend to express a preference for staying in their homes and adapting to climate change, as demonstrated by Maldives.

item.title: "A Rusting Metal Behemoth, Within the Crumbling Masonry of Empire": Addressing Sugar Plantations as Sites of Forgetting on the Island of Saint Lucia | Published in Island Studies Journal
item.description: By Arun Sood, Marenka Thompson-Odlum & 1 more. Spanning archaeology, oral history, poetry, sound studies, archival research, and community co-curation, this case study shows how multidisciplinary approaches can reevaluate neglected landscapes that have become ‘sites of forgetting’
